scope: Proposition 7.7 (The finite-horizon cube success bound) of the manuscript “Localization costs and information growth for exact Gaussian observations” (preprints/Localization-costs-and-information-growth-for-exact-Gaussian-observations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f43e1443f9fd513), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For sufficiently large d, consider a deterministic Borel computation padded to m ≥ 0 blocks of n rows as above. Suppose its boundary alphabet has size at most N, where N1/k ≤ 2d, and its final boundary state fixes its unit output. Its average success under (69) is at most ∆m + 22Ddm (5ϵ)p , ∆m = 3m2−c1d + 2−d m−1 X t=0 (⌊Jt⌋ + 1). (88) The sum is empty when m = 0. In particular, ∆m = o(1) for any sequence m = o(d).
